What if I told you that the word "salary" is connected to something sitting in your kitchen right now?
Yes, the same salt you put on your food.
But thousands of years ago, salt was much more valuable than it is today.
People needed salt to preserve meat and other foods so they wouldn't spoil.
And in ancient Rome, salt was so important that it became connected to the way people talked about payment.
The Latin word "salarium" eventually gave us the English word "salary."
There's even a famous story that Roman soldiers were paid in salt.
But historians haven't found solid evidence that soldiers actually received salt instead of money.
Still, the connection between salt and salary is real.
So next time your paycheck arrives, remember…
A word we use for earning money today has its roots in an ancient everyday ingredient.
You didn't know that about money!
